Topic: J-ICS Lifer Super-Long Re-Entry = 2-3yr Portfolio Rollover, NOT a Yield Level
Key_Fact: Under the J-ICS solvency regime, getting life insurers back into super-long JGBs is a 2-3yr portfolio-rollover process, NOT a matter of yields reaching a buying floor. Mechanism: rising yields mark down legacy low-coupon holdings *first* (hurting ESR/solvency buffers) before higher reinvestment yields help — so the lifer bid is buffer-conditional. Re-entry requires legacy 0.2-0.5% coupons maturing or sold and reinvested at current 3.5-3.9%, slowly lifting book yields; "compensation has improved, optionality has not" (Vedanjanam, Aviva Investors 2026). Consequence: no yield near current 30Y ~3.76% draws lifers back within a tradeable window; demand-vacuum is structural, multi-quarter, not yield-sensitive near term.
